answer: Agents requiring expensive computational terraces atop karst formations—unique geological structures demanding ocean-scale energy investments—prevent Sybil attacks. Each virtual persona must process real-time sensor data from geographically constrained installations, making identity replication prohibitively costly. Karst terrain's inaccessibility forces attackers to invest in physical infrastructure, while ocean energy grids ensure verification costs scale with computational demand. This mechanism leverages geography and resource scarcity to enforce proof-of-presence protocols.
